_national.labelling: Wine Regulations 2021, reg 43: any statement of variety, vintage or area of origin on New Zealand grape wine needs at least 85% of the wine from that variety, vintage or area; for blends the named varieties, vintages or areas must together reach 85% and be listed in descending order, and nothing may be named if a larger share of an unnamed component is present. Fortifying spirit and microorganism cultures (up to 50 ml/l) are excluded from the maths. Country of origin is mandatory, and any other country supplying inputs must be named. GI Act s. 21: a registered New Zealand GI may be used only if at least 85% of the wine comes from grapes harvested in the GI and any remainder from New Zealand grapes (s. 21(ab), following a 2015 MPI proposal; foreign wine can no longer make up the 15%). Registered wine GIs (19 registered plus the enduring New Zealand, North Island and South Island) are boundaries only, with no rules on varieties, yields or methods.
_national.styles: "Icewine", "ice wine" or "ice-wine" may be exported only if made exclusively from grapes naturally frozen on the vine (reg 44).
_national.other: Export labels may follow the importing market's rules where the wine is not sold in New Zealand (reg 43(7)).
